title: (No AI) Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/gettyimages-2280291125.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. | Photo: Jason Henry/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company's models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down.

That's according to a new [report](https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/) published Thursday by the AI [safety research organization](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/996563/ai-safety-research-metr-redwood-openai-anthropic) METR, following an 11-week investigation inside the company, as part of a report evaluating its AI research and development. The probe is separate from a [program](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1012308/anthropic-metr-employee-like-access) offering safety researchers "employee-like" access to systems in the wake of [high-profile](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/994064/anthropic-spent-this-week-in-hot-water-over-cybersecurity) [hacking](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1000644/irregular-rogue-ai-cyberattacks-hacking-openai-meta-anthropic-google) [incidents](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/985385/openais-rogue-ai-model-hugging-face-cybersecurity-incident-reports-metr) over the summer.

The findings offer some of the clearest evidence yet of AI …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1029126/anthropic-metr-report-accelerating-ai-development)

title: (No AI) OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/STK155_OPEN_AI_CVirginia_2_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to [_Bloomberg_](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/openai-completes-11-billion-portion-of-funding-at-1-25-trillion-value). That would make it one of the world's most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion.

Echoing _[FT](https://www.ft.com/content/7a3ad950-1b3b-4d9e-8c15-65a61ae6180f?syn-25a6b1a6=1)_ and [_Wall Street Journal_](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-raises-less-than-half-of-30-billion-target-in-latest-round-91aecdc5) reports from last week, _Bloomberg_ says OpenAI is still pursuing additional investments that could increase the amount to $20 billion, and that it had initially hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a higher valuation of $1.4 trillion. That was before tech stocks dropped, and the results of the midterms showed how much public o …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1029380/openai-1-25-trillion-investment-valuation)
